what_this_is: Divergences between a published page and the version the ledger records, that somebody has looked at and deliberately decided not to close yet. NOT publications. The guard still prints a line for each, saying it is known; it prints the full warning again the moment the live content changes by one byte, because each entry is bound to a content hash rather than to an issue.
the_rule: An entry here is a decision to leave something outstanding, with a name and a reason on it. It can never cover a divergence the current push is CREATING -- that path blocks, and this file is not consulted there. It only quiets a divergence that already existed.

acknowledged.reason: Issue two is live at a version the ledger does not record, and closing it properly costs money we have decided not to spend on a prototype nobody subscribed to. The whole difference is one word: 'Jacot and colleagues' corrected to 'Tanguy and colleagues', who are the paper's actual authors. The live page is therefore MORE correct than the signed-off one, which is why leaving it is tolerable.
acknowledged.what_it_would_take_to_close: publish.py publish cdk46 --yes, blocked by: a fresh page gate, a fresh email gate, four outside-review changes with no decision, seven unknowability claims naming no registry, a counterexample hunt on twelve universal negatives, one quoted claim printed as our own, and the dateline. Two cost money. Deliberately not being done: issue two is a prototype with no subscribers and the lessons have been taken into the process instead.
acknowledged.this_is_not: a record that issue two has been republished. It has not been.
